races.paceDynamic: Salvator Mundi and Mighty Bandit will ensure a genuine gallop from the outset, with both confirmed front-runners likely to dispute the early lead over this sharp 2-mile trip. The honest pace they set will stretch the field and create pressure throughout, particularly on the testing going conditions. With limited cover available and the pace likely to be relentless, prominent racers who can track the leaders without getting embroiled in the early battle hold a clear tactical advantage. This race shape strongly favours prominent runners who can position close enough to strike but avoid the early speed duel.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the two leaders engage in a sustained battle from halfway, burning each other out
scenarios.body: The honest gallop perfectly sets up horses tracking in third or fourth, allowing them to pick up the pieces when the pace-setters weaken. Be Aware and Kala Conti are ideally positioned to exploit this dynamic.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader Survives Battle
scenarios.trigger: If one of Salvator Mundi or Mighty Bandit can establish a clear advantage and dictate terms
scenarios.body: The winner gets first run on their rivals and maintains just enough in reserve to repel late challengers on ground that will sap stamina. Strong jumping becomes crucial to maintain momentum.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Benefits
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes truly ferocious and the field comes back to the closers
scenarios.body: No Questions Asked can use his patient tactics to devastating effect, picking off tired leaders in the final furlong. The soft ground will amplify the effects of early pace pressure.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the two main pace-setters are slower to engage than expected, creating a more sedate tempo
scenarios.body: This allows the patient runners to get closer than anticipated while keeping something in reserve for a sustained finish. The race becomes more about class than tactics.

watchPoints.text: Salvator Mundi and Mighty Bandit engaging in early speed duel could set up the race for patient trackers
Kala Conti's fitness after 70-day break despite being highest-rated runner in the field
No Questions Asked getting closer to the pace than usual if the early gallop is moderate
King Of Kingsfield's jumping after 134 days off and whether Danny Gilligan can get him competitive from the start
Be Aware's ability to position perfectly behind the two leaders without getting caught in their battle

races.paceDynamic: Push The Button, Fortune Timmy, and Hold The Serve will force a strong gallop from the start, with Fortune Timmy's recent wins showing he's in good order to sustain the pace. The 22-runner field creates a traffic nightmare through the middle stages, with 9 prominent racers fighting for position behind the leaders. This sets up perfectly for the patient hold-up horses like Jeriko Du Reponet, Ace Of Spades, and Harbour Lake who can avoid the scrimmaging and unleash late runs. The combination of strong early pace and prominent congestion strongly favours hold-up horses with tactical speed.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the front three go too fast and the prominent pack gets congested turning for home
scenarios.body: The pace collapses as leaders tire and traffic develops, allowing the patient runners clear runs to sweep past tired horses. Hold-up specialists with class can pick off the field systematically.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tactical Success
scenarios.trigger: If one or two prominent runners can secure ideal positions without getting trapped
scenarios.body: They avoid both the early pace burn and the late traffic, timing their moves perfectly as leaders weaken. The tactical prominent horses get first run on the tiring pace-setters.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If Fortune Timmy or Hold The Serve can control the tempo and kick clear before the closers arrive
scenarios.body: The leader dictates a more manageable pace than expected, staying strong enough to resist the late challenge. Class and stamina prevail over pure tactics.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Completely
scenarios.trigger: If all three leaders go too hard early and burn out spectacularly before halfway
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint from the back as no horse wants to go forward, suiting the strongest late finisher. Pure class and acceleration decide the winner.

watchPoints.text: Fortune Timmy and Hold The Serve must not let Push The Button dictate the early tempo or all three leaders could go too fast
Absolutely Doyen and Supremely West need to secure prominent positions early before the field bunches approaching the home turn
Jeriko Du Reponet requires a strong pace and clear run from the back to be effective in this large field
Harbour Lake's 100-day absence and jumping reliability after such a break needs monitoring
Bold Endeavour wearing cheekpieces for first time suggests connections think he needs more pace engagement

races.paceDynamic: Montemares, Masked Man, and Came From Nowhere will ensure a strong gallop from the outset, with all three natural front-runners likely to dispute the early lead. This relentless pace will stretch the field and test stamina reserves over the testing 2m4f trip on soft ground at Aintree. The sustained gallop will suit horses with proven staying power who can finish strongly from off the pace. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses and patient riders who can capitalize on the inevitable pace collapse.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners maintain a fierce gallop through the middle stages
scenarios.body: The leaders will weaken dramatically from the second-last hurdle, allowing closers with superior stamina to surge past tired rivals. Hold-up performers like Bossman Jack and Soldier Reeves are perfectly positioned to exploit this scenario.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Tactical Battle Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If one of the front-runners drops back early, reducing the overall tempo
scenarios.body: A more measured pace allows prominent racers to conserve energy and kick clear from the final hurdle. Ballyfad and Rooster Crowing can position perfectly to strike when the race develops.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If Montemares or Came From Nowhere gets a soft lead after rivals fall away
scenarios.body: The leader maintains enough in reserve to repel late challenges on ground that suits their style. Their recent form suggests the ability to dictate from the front successfully.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Suits Midfield
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuine but not suicidal, allowing tactical positioning
scenarios.body: Horses settling in fourth or fifth can time their runs perfectly without being caught too far back. This narrow window requires perfect judgment from experienced jockeys.

watchPoints.text: Montemares could get an uncontested lead if Masked Man and Came From Nowhere fail to go early pace
Soldier Reeves offers strong each-way value if the pace sets up perfectly for his finishing kick
Ballyfad's prominent style could be negated entirely if the three leaders set a furious early gallop
Lord Byron's poor recent form makes him vulnerable despite his each-way appeal on ratings
Charisma Cat's weight allowance could prove crucial in a tight finish between the hold-up horses

races.paceDynamic: Lookaway and the declared runners will set honest early fractions in this competitive handicap chase over testing ground. With one confirmed front-runner in Lookaway, expect a solid gallop from the start that will string out the 18-runner field early. The good-to-soft conditions and 3m1f trip will create a stamina test where horses need to be positioned handily turning for home. This race shape strongly favours prominent runners and those with tactical pace who can avoid traffic problems in a large field.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Honest Gallop Holds
scenarios.trigger: If Lookaway maintains a solid tempo without going too fast early
scenarios.body: The pace will be genuine but sustainable, allowing prominent runners to stay in touch and kick when it matters. Hold-up horses will find it difficult to make up ground in the large field on testing ground.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Strong Early Pace
scenarios.trigger: If multiple prominent runners press Lookaway and force a stronger early tempo
scenarios.body: The increased pace will set up the race for closers who can stay the trip and have the class to pick up the pieces. The testing conditions will amplify the effects of the early exertions.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Muddling Early Pace
scenarios.trigger: If Lookaway is allowed an easy lead with little early pressure
scenarios.body: The race will become a sprint finish where tactical positioning matters most and those closest to the pace hold the advantage. Prominent runners with a turn of foot will benefit from the lack of early tempo.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Traffic Problems
scenarios.trigger: If the large field causes significant interference or bunching at key moments
scenarios.body: Running room becomes crucial and those able to secure clear passages will have major advantages over equally talented rivals who get hampered. Early positioning will prove vital.

watchPoints.text: Lookaway must be watched early as the lone confirmed front-runner could dictate proceedings entirely
Uncle Bert carries just 160lbs with a 5lb claimer and could be overpriced after his course win
Bad and Leave Of Absence both hold strong chances if they can secure good positions early
Traffic problems are likely in this 18-runner field so early positioning will be crucial
Deep Cave needs a strong pace to collapse but has winning form at exactly this trip

races.paceDynamic: Hiddenvalley Lake will set the pace with minimal early pressure, creating a controlled gallop over this stamina test. Strong Leader, Honesty Policy and Jingko Blue will track prominently, but none will apply significant pressure to the leader early. The lack of genuine pace pressure means the race will develop into a tactical affair where positioning becomes crucial approaching the business end. This scenario strongly favours hold-up horses who can produce sustained finishing kicks, as the moderate early pace will leave plenty in reserve for those coming from behind.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Heroes Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Hiddenvalley Lake is allowed to dictate a modest pace without serious challenge
scenarios.body: The tactical nature allows hold-up specialists to position perfectly and unleash devastating late runs when the pace quickens. Home By The Lee and Impose Toi benefit most from this patient setup with their proven finishing kicks.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pressure Pays
scenarios.trigger: If Strong Leader or Honesty Policy decide to challenge Hiddenvalley Lake earlier than expected
scenarios.body: The increased tempo stretches the field and prevents hold-up horses from closing effectively. Those already in striking positions can capitalize on their forward placement.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Tactical Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the field remains bunched turning for home with multiple horses still on the bridle
scenarios.body: A mad dash develops over the final two furlongs where class and tactical speed matter most. The highest-rated horses with good positioning edge out those caught wide or flat-footed.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Hiddenvalley Lake goes too slow and the field becomes strung out with stop-start fractions
scenarios.body: The race turns into a messy affair where horses with tactical pace rather than pure class can steal it. Those able to adapt quickly to the changing rhythm gain the advantage.

watchPoints.text: Hiddenvalley Lake setting too slow a pace early could create tactical chaos that derails market leaders
Strong Leader's 77-day absence after good recent form - watch for fitness versus freshness factor
Home By The Lee's jumping under pressure in the final mile given his hold-up style reliance
Impose Toi's position turning for home as Henderson horses often need good early positioning
Take No Chances and Lavida Adiva carrying 7lbs less weight could be significant in tactical finish

races.name: Randox Grand National Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: I Am Maximus
runners_data.note: Hold-up style perfectly suits this pace scenario, defending champion with excellent soft ground record and Townend knows these fences intimately
runners_data.comment: 1st and 2nd in last two Grand Nationals; penultimate race suggests all his ability remains
runners_data.spotlight: His only three long-distance events resulted in an Irish National win in 2023, a storming success in this race in 2024 (soft) and a valiant second, from further off the pace, to Nick Rockett on return to Aintree in 2025 (good to soft); what a record that is, and 50-1 second in a 3m Grade 1 at Leopardstown on penultimate start gives every encouragement that all his ability remains; the return of cheekpieces (tried once in 2022) is interesting but, off 1lb higher than last year, he should be set for another prominent finish.

runners_data.name: Nick Rockett
runners_data.comment: Won this in 2025 in basically smooth style; up 4lb; this year's preparation is a big worry
runners_data.spotlight: Final leg of last season's hat-trick was delivered in basically smooth style here in the National, asserting in the final 1f from I Am Maximus and Grangeclare West (good to soft); 4lb higher today but it's far more concerning that his season has hardly got going, with reappearance delayed until last month when he was seriously ring-rusty behind Gerri Colombe; last year's and this year's build-ups could hardly be more contrasting and he's been deserted by Patrick Mullins.

runners_data.name: Gerri Colombe
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who needs to avoid early pace battle, Gold Cup class but form below best this season
runners_data.comment: 2nd in 2024 Cheltenham Gold Cup and, some positive signs lately, could be on his way back
runners_data.spotlight: Five Grade 1 wins and runner-up in the 2024 Cheltenham Gold Cup; reappearance at Christmas came after 421 days off and this season's form is well short of his best, but second to Grangeclare West at Fairyhouse was a big step back in the right direction and he comfortably obliged at odds-on for latest outing; cheekpieces last three starts; well handicapped on his old form and could be on his way back.

runners_data.name: Monty's Star
runners_data.note: Prominent style but lacks a win in 11 chase starts, fourth in Gold Cup shows stamina but needs career-best
runners_data.comment: Trying in vain at Grade 1 level; going up markedly in trip in a handicap is mouthwatering
runners_data.spotlight: Just 1-11 as a chaser, largely because he keeps trying in vain at Grade 1 level; fourth in last year's Cheltenham Gold Cup was one of his peak efforts, as was this season's never-nearer fifth in a Leopardstown Grade 1 at Christmas; he didn't fare so well in the Irish Gold Cup last time but was the only one matching strides with the top-class winner on the home turn; going up markedly in trip today, in a handicap, makes him a mouthwatering proposition.

runners_data.name: Champ Kiely
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner making debut at this trip, likely to set strong pace but stamina untested beyond 3m1f
runners_data.comment: Whether he'll stay 4m2f is a big question but he could outrun his odds for a long way
runners_data.spotlight: The furthest he's been is 3m1f in Grade 1 novice at Punchestown Festival (good to yielding) last April which he won in good style, showing improved form; went close over 2m in November and although he slipped up next time and met with heavy defeats twice since, he went well enough to the home turn in Irish Gold Cup on latest; whether he'll stay 4m2f is a big question but he could outrun his odds for a long way.

runners_data.name: Firefox
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with tongue-tie fitted, proven at this trip in Irish Gold Cup and suits the expected strong pace
runners_data.comment: Ran on late when fourth in Irish Gold Cup (3m); didn't see out 3m2f so well at Cheltenham
runners_data.spotlight: Tongue tied on last two starts; first time he went beyond 2m5f was also in the Irish Gold Cup at Leopardstown (3m, soft) in February, when 33-1 and spending most of the race out the back but running on into fourth of 12, beaten 14l; some encouragement might be derived from that but he didn't see it out so well when confronted by 3m2f in the Gold Cup at Cheltenham.

runners_data.name: Spillane's Tower
runners_data.comment: Won Grade 2 Cotswold Chase; others have achieved more but he's open to further improvement
runners_data.spotlight: Won two Grade 1s in Ireland in spring 2024 during novice chase campaign (2m4f/3m1f, heavy/yielding) and posted first win since in the Grade 2 Cotswold Chase at Cheltenham (3m1f, soft) this January; he was receiving 6lb from close runner-up L'Homme Presse last time and others in this have achieved more, but he's only eight and could still have improvement to come.

runners_data.name: Oscars Brother
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner trained by small stable, hat-trick winner with excellent form but lacks Grand National experience
runners_data.comment: Slow early jumping in 3m1f Grade 1 novice at Cheltenham but he made late inroads into 4th
runners_data.spotlight: A first-season novice won the 2022 Grand National when unraced beyond 3m1f and this Irish challenger (who's one year older) bids to repeat the feat; hat-trick this season included two small-field Grade 2s and when his winning sequence came to an end it was in the Grade 1 novice at Cheltenham Festival, where some slow jumping in the early stages left him with plenty to do but he made late inroads to finish fourth; he still looks capable of better and the longer trip could suit.

runners_data.name: Jordans
runners_data.note: Hold-up style suits, twice Grade 1 placed over staying trips but needs to bounce back from poor recent form
runners_data.comment: Second in the 3m1f Grade 1 novice chase at this meeting last year; below form since
runners_data.spotlight: Twice second in Grade 1 novice events last season, most notably when upped substantially in trip to 3m1f at this meeting; possibilities judged on that performance (unraced over further) and although he's been nowhere near that form since, his closest finish this term came when a staying-on fifth of 18 over 2m7f as a hurdler; just a 7yo but not totally dismissed.

runners_data.name: Iroko
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who was fourth in last year's National, tongue-tie applied and well-positioned for another big run
runners_data.comment: Staying-on fourth in 2025 National off 5lb lower; scoped dirty at Cheltenham last month
runners_data.spotlight: Staying-on fourth in last season's Grand National (good to soft) off 5lb lower as just a 7yo; a second crack at it has been his main target this term but he looked better than ever when winning from Firefox in a hot, three-runner race at Ascot (2m5f; second run after wind surgery) in December and had an excuse (scoped dirty) at the Cheltenham Festival last month; has to be in serious calculations.

runners_data.name: The Real Whacker
runners_data.note: Prominent style but 100 days since last run creates fitness doubts despite being well-handicapped
runners_data.comment: Well handicapped on peak efforts but those past glories may now be too distant
runners_data.spotlight: 11lb below his peak mark and well handicapped judged on best efforts, the most recent of which were over 3m on good ground late in 2024; muted in this three runs this term, only one of which was over fences but he ended up tailed off in that Wetherby race, which he'd won a year earlier; those past glories may now be too distant.

runners_data.name: Quai De Bourbon
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with cheekpieces fitted, Irish National third shows stamina but inconsistent jumping record
runners_data.comment: Third in the 3m5f Irish National last April but completed only four of his eight chases
runners_data.spotlight: Third in the 3m5f Irish National last April, despite an indifferent round of jumping, and third of 16 with cheekpieces at Leopardstown on latest outing was his best form, despite just the 2m5f; kept jumping out to his right in the latter and although a case can be made for him, it would have to gloss over that he's completed only four of his eight chases.

runners_data.name: Grangeclare West
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who was excellent third last year, amateur rider Patrick Mullins takes valuable 7lb allowance
runners_data.comment: 3l third last year, after diving at the final fence (up 3lb today); won his latest outing
runners_data.spotlight: Excellent 3l third to Nick Rockett in last year's renewal, somehow renewing his effort after diving at the final fence cost him plenty of momentum; creditable fifth at Sandown just three weeks later and surging clear from Gerri Colombe at Fairyhouse this February, after another last-fence dive, showed that he's at least as good as ever; 3lb higher than 12 months ago but lots to like.

runners_data.name: Johnnywho
runners_data.note: Hold-up style with cheekpieces and tongue-tie fitted, excellent over these fences but Irish National form disappointing
runners_data.comment: 2nd and 1st over 3m2f/3m1f at Cheltenham Festivals and wasn't stopping; up 6lb in future
runners_data.spotlight: Fine over these fences in November; laboured from before three out when a well-beaten fifth to Haiti Couleurs in Irish National last April; that was in the mud, though, and his top efforts have been on good to soft; they include his neck second in the 3m2f Kim Muir at Cheltenham last March and, equipped with first-time cheekpieces after wind surgery, a 3m1f win from Jagwar at this year's Festival; able to race here off the same mark as last time (due to go up 6lb) and he wasn't stopping in either of those big races at Cheltenham; seriously considered.

runners_data.name: High Class Hero
runners_data.note: Front-runner who will help set strong pace, Sandown staying form promising but recent heavy ground efforts poor
runners_data.comment: Staying-on third over an extended 3m4f at Sandown (good; 5lb higher today) last April
runners_data.spotlight: One positive is his staying-on third over an extended 3m4f in the bet365 Gold Cup at Sandown (good; 5lb higher today) last April; another is that he's trained by Willie Mullins, who described him in November as likely to be "an ideal type for the Grand National"; after a solid reappearance, he's been pulled up in good handicaps on his last two outings but both were in the mud and he got loose before the latest, which presumably didn't help.

runners_data.name: Captain Cody
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 49-day break, Leopardstown form gives hope but needs significant improvement
runners_data.comment: Tremendous response on the run-in to win 4m Scottish National last April; 12lb higher now
runners_data.spotlight: Leopardstown seventh to Favori De Champdou at Christmas was a glimpse of what he's capable of; the performance which really gets the juices flowing, however, came in the Scottish National at Ayr (4m, good to soft) last April when very confidently ridden and unleashed to find a tremendous response on the run-in, cutting down the leader; it's very hard to rule him out after that, despite the 12lb higher mark.

runners_data.name: Jagwar
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with cheekpieces and tongue-tie, progressive chaser making debut at this extreme trip
runners_data.comment: Constant improver; went close when upped to 3m1f at Cheltenham after some jumping errors
runners_data.spotlight: Improved his rating in every one of his eight chases, winning four and that includes the 2m4f Plate at last year's Cheltenham Festival; first venture much beyond 2m5f had to wait until his return to Cheltenham last month, in which he came from out the back to get within half a length of the winner Johnnywho; that showed he stays 3m1f and suggested he's still capable of better, but his jumping contained unnerving moments; wears cheekpieces first time and a half-brother probably stays 4m.

runners_data.name: Banbridge
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with visor fitted, King George second shows class but quick ground specialist may struggle
runners_data.comment: So nearly won his second King George at Kempton, which doesn't mean this test will suit
runners_data.spotlight: So nearly won his second King George at Kempton over Christmas but, although he's a class act, excelling over 3m on good ground at that speed track doesn't mean that this test will suit him; his moderate late headway in the extended 2m4f Grade 1 Ryanair at Cheltenham last month isn't that persuasive either.

runners_data.name: Imperial Saint
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who is reserve, three wins over these conventional fences but may not get a run
runners_data.comment: 3 wins over conventional fences here; 3m1f win this January but this trip is a big unknown
runners_data.spotlight: Reserve; novice campaign last season went well, notably over the conventional fences here where he registered three handicap wins (2m/2m4f) and was second at this meeting (3m1f); resumed progress with a win at Haydock (3m1f) this January but badly hampered at the Cheltenham Festival; this trip is a big step into the unknown but he needs a second look.

runners_data.name: Stellar Story
runners_data.note: Prominent style with tongue-tie and blinkers, Grade 1 novice form excellent but winter efforts disappointing
runners_data.comment: Unraced beyond 3m2f but has strongly suggested that he has serious stamina; e-w appeal
runners_data.spotlight: Second to Lecky Watson in the 3m Grade 1 novice at Cheltenham last March; while comfortably dismissed in the closing stages of his three starts this winter, the first two of those were Grade 1 events and giving 8lb to Grangeclare West and Gerri Colombe at Fairyhouse (blinkers replaced cheekpieces) on latest outing makes that result look a whole lot better; above all, perhaps, while unraced beyond 3m2f, he has strongly suggested on plenty of occasions that he has serious stamina reserves; each-way appeal.

runners_data.name: Answer To Kayf
runners_data.note: Prominent runner from small stable, won good 3m handicap but faded over longer at Punchestown
runners_data.comment: Faded in a 3m7f race; clearly his best five ratings were registered on soft or heavy going
runners_data.spotlight: Faded into sixth at Punchestown (3m7f) last May on his only attempt at a marathon trip; worth another go, having rallied so well to win a major 3m handicap at Navan in November, but it's a little hard to ignore that clearly his best five ratings have been registered on soft or heavy going, as have all his four wins.

runners_data.name: Lecky Watson
runners_data.note: Prominent runner making debut beyond 3m2f, Cheltenham Festival winner but poor form this season
runners_data.comment: Won 3m Grade 1 at Cheltenham last March from Stellar Story; no impact in Ireland this term
runners_data.spotlight: Unraced beyond 3m2f; came into his own as a novice last term, notably in the 3m Grade 1 at Cheltenham Festival which he won by 4l from Stellar Story; no impact at the top level in Ireland this season and he clambered over the final fence on his way to a heavy defeat behind several of today's rivals in a Grade 3 last time, so current prospects don't look so bright.

runners_data.name: Mr Vango
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with cheekpieces and tongue-tie, Midlands National winner but close second in Becher suggests vulnerable
runners_data.comment: Nothing to prove for stamina or this track, but he cracked alarmingly on last two outings
runners_data.spotlight: Last season's hat-trick culminated in the 4m2f Midlands National and he rallied to go very close against Twig in the 3m2f Becher over these fences on first outing this term; while there was so much to admire to that point, he's cracked with alarming speed in 3m and 4m1f races on his last two outings.

runners_data.name: Three Card Brag
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with cheekpieces, excellent autumn form including Cheltenham win but flopped at Christmas
runners_data.comment: Career-best form in the autumn; last year's Grand National and latest start are concerns
runners_data.spotlight: Career-best form in the autumn this season, including a win at Cheltenham (3m1f) and second to Panic Attack in the Coral Gold Cup at Newbury (3m2f); flopped when favourite in the Grade 3 won by Grangeclare West at Fairyhouse in February, admittedly after 12 weeks off but there's the additional worry of last year's Grand National in which he was 16-1 and raced very prominently but faded steadily from three out.

runners_data.name: Panic Attack
runners_data.note: Prominent style and in career-best form, dual November winner but 10-year-old making debut at this extreme distance
runners_data.comment: 8lb higher than for her big-race win at Newbury (3m2f) but her dominance is hard to forget
runners_data.spotlight: 10yo who is better than ever this term, including with a big handicap double in November in the Paddy Power Gold Cup at Cheltenham (2m4f, soft) and Coral Gold Cup at Newbury (3m2f, good to soft); dropping back to 2m4f, however, was probably not ideal when creditable third in mares' race at Cheltenham last month; 8lb higher than in the Newbury race but her dominance that day is hard to forget.

runners_data.name: Haiti Couleurs
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with multiple marathon wins including Welsh National, 12lb higher than Welsh National victory
runners_data.comment: Irish and Welsh National winner; Gold Cup was disappointing but he's bounced back before
runners_data.spotlight: In the last 13 months he's won Cheltenham's NH Chase (3m6f), the Irish National (3m5f), a hurdle race, Welsh National (near 3m7f; 12lb higher today) and a Newbury Grade 2; no way can he be ruled out, particularly as he finished well on top in those four chases, but there have also been two major blips this season; latest was in the Cheltenham Gold Cup, for which he was just 6-1 and made most but went to nothing turning for home (writing on the wall four out); however, he's bounced back before, the likely tempo of this race can suit him better and the trip looks like doing so as well.

runners_data.name: Gorgeous Tom
runners_data.note: Front-runner who will set strong pace, Grade 1 fourth behind these rivals shows ability but needs career-best
runners_data.comment: 11l fourth off this mark to Panic Attack at Newbury (3m2f) and stuck to his task very well
runners_data.spotlight: Fourth behind two of these in 3m Grade 1 novice event at Cheltenham last March; ran creditably all three starts this winter, notably 11l fourth of 24 off this mark to Panic Attack at Newbury (3m2f) in November when he stuck to his task very well having been left at the shambolic start; improvement is needed but that race gave encouragement for longer trips and his dam is half-sister to Cappa Bleu who was placed in this race in 2012 and 2013.

runners_data.name: Top Of The Bill
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with cheekpieces, veteran in career-best form but 56 days since last run raises fitness questions
runners_data.comment: An excellent, rallying second at Haydock (extended 3m4f) but this is a much stronger race
runners_data.spotlight: One of several who are now in the veteran stage but also in the form of their lives; 7l winner at Haydock (extended 3m1f) in November and returned there with an excellent, rallying second in the Grand National Trial (extended 3m4f, again good to soft) in February; ridden last three starts by Toby McCain-Mitchell; back up 2lb and an interesting prospect for 4m2f but this is a much stronger race.

runners_data.name: Beauport
runners_data.note: Prominent style with tongue-tie, won Midlands National but faded quickly over these fences last year
runners_data.comment: Stays but he was too zestful in this race last year; now tongue tied first time
runners_data.spotlight: Took well to these fences in last year's renewal but subsided rapidly after three out, which might have been surprising for one who'd won a 4m2f Midlands National (March 2024) but he seemed to race a bit too zestfully in the front rank; 3lb lower today, having run respectably on reappearance but moderately in two hurdle races since (wind surgery before latest); now tongue tied first time; a bit to prove.

runners_data.name: Marble Sands
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who is 106 days since last run, Cheltenham winner but huge fitness question
runners_data.comment: A strong-staying winner at Cheltenham (near 3m4f, soft; 5lb higher today) in November
runners_data.spotlight: Negotiated these fences safely in the 2m5f Topham one year ago, albeit fading into 12th; a strong-staying display to win at Cheltenham (near 3m4f, soft; 5lb higher today) in November hints at untapped potential over long distances.

runners_data.name: Perceval Legallois
runners_data.note: Hold-up style but fell at third fence in last year's National, 100 days since last run creates major fitness doubt
runners_data.comment: Joint-third fav for this in 2025 but fell at the ninth; nothing to shout about this winter
runners_data.spotlight: Won major 3m handicaps at Leopardstown over fences (by 7l, going away) and hurdles before starting joint-third favourite for last year's National, but he fell on the first circuit; it's too early to forget his best performance (Christmas 2024) but with nothing to shout about in his two races this winter, this time he could be an outsider.

runners_data.name: Twig
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with cheekpieces, 11-year-old beat Mr Vango in Becher but age and trip combination demanding
runners_data.comment: A doughty 3m2f win over these fences in the Becher but remote 10th in last year's National
runners_data.spotlight: Second at the 2024 Cheltenham Festival and started this season with two wins, notably by a short head from Mr Vango in the 3m2f Becher over these fences (wore cheekpieces second time); warmed up for this over hurdles after three months off; the Becher performance was doughty stuff but his only go at a marathon trip was last year's National in which he finished a remote tenth, always behind.

runners_data.name: Spanish Harlem
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with cheekpieces and tongue-tie, form upturn this season but pulled up in last two starts
runners_data.comment: Stays long distances; his revised mark since bold show in the Thyestes is the chief worry
runners_data.spotlight: Career with Willie Mullins took a long time to catch fire but it's done so this season and he looked set for victory in the Thyestes at Gowran Park (3m1f, heavy) in January when unseating at the final fence; pulled up behind Grangeclare West last time but back catalogue includes a creditable sixth in the Scottish National and fourth in bet365 Cup at Sandown, so he stays long distances; his revised mark since the Thyestes would be the chief worry.

runners_data.name: Pied Piper
runners_data.comment: Outbattled over 3m1f in October; it's doubtful whether he's got what it takes for this
runners_data.spotlight: Gained all three chase wins in small-field novice events last April-June (one over 2m7f) but fell in three of his nine races since, including the last two; placed over 2m1f as a hurdler at three Cheltenham Festivals and runner-up in a 2m2f Cesarewitch on Flat, but he was outbattled over 3m1f at Cheltenham in October; it's doubtful whether he's got what it takes for this.

runners_data.name: Favori De Champdou
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with blinkers, 11-year-old having excellent season but age and distance combination challenging
runners_data.comment: 11yo who's having a tremendous season, over Cheltenham cross-country on last two outings
runners_data.spotlight: Experienced 11yo who's having a tremendous season; 66-1 winner of a top 3m handicap at Leopardstown (made most) over Christmas and took his form to another new level on the 3m5f Cheltenham cross-country course on last two outings, winning easily on first occasion and well clear of the third when he chased home Final Orders at last month's Festival; well handicapped and with the trip likely to suit, he's a leading contender.

runners_data.name: Final Orders
runners_data.note: Prominent style from 10-year-old with 70 career runs, cross-country Festival winner shows stamina and experience
runners_data.comment: Has taken so well to Cheltenham cross-country; best performances away from soft ground
runners_data.spotlight: 10yo who's had 70 races (only one of today's rivals has managed even half that) and won 11; latest was the 3m5f cross-country at Cheltenham Festival, comfortably holding off Favori De Champdou for career-best form off the same mark as today; having taken so well to that discipline (he also won there in December) and produced his best performances away from soft ground, he has to be considered seriously.

runners_data.name: Amirite
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who is reserve with tongue-tie, fourth in Topham over these fences but may not get a run
runners_data.comment: A fluent fourth in the Topham over these fences last April; ran creditably once at 3m4f
runners_data.spotlight: Reserve; a fluent fourth in the 2m5f Topham over these fences was the first of three big runs in good handicaps last April-July; ran creditably in one (Sandown in April 2024) of his three attempts at 3m4f-3m5f and excuses might be made for his latest two outings (first cross-country, then the mud) but other candidates are more persuasive.

races.paceDynamic: Champ Kiely, High Class Hero, Mr Vango and Gorgeous Tom will ensure a strong gallop from the start, with Haiti Couleurs, Panic Attack and Banbridge also wanting to be handy early. This creates a searching test of stamina over the marathon trip, with the relentless pace likely to string out the field significantly by halfway. The prominent brigade faces congestion issues with 15+ runners wanting that position, creating traffic problems at the business end. This pace scenario heavily favours the hold-up horses who can pick off tired leaders, particularly those with proven stamina at extreme distances.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-up horses dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the strong early pace creates the expected stamina test and prominent runners get into trouble
scenarios.body: The relentless gallop set by multiple front-runners will take its toll, allowing patient riders on proven stayers to sweep past tired leaders in the final mile. Horses like I Am Maximus, Firefox and Jagwar can exploit this perfectly with their come-from-behind styles.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent tactical winner
scenarios.trigger: If one of the handy horses can find the perfect position without getting caught in the early pace battle
scenarios.body: A horse like Gerri Colombe or Monty's Star could sit just off the pace setters, avoid the early burn-up, and have enough left to outrun the closers. The key is positioning third or fourth early rather than disputing the lead.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-runner survives
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is more measured than expected due to tactical jockeying
scenarios.body: Haiti Couleurs or Mr Vango could dictate terms from the front and have enough stamina reserves to repel late challenges. Their marathon experience gives them the edge if they can control the tempo.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos benefits outsider
scenarios.trigger: If multiple fallers and traffic problems eliminate many fancied runners
scenarios.body: The Grand National's unpredictable nature could see a lesser-fancied horse with a clear passage benefit from others' misfortunes. Horses like Final Orders or Marble Sands have the experience to capitalize on carnage.

watchPoints.text: Multiple front-runners including Champ Kiely, High Class Hero, Mr Vango and Gorgeous Tom will create a searching early pace that could burn out prominent horses caught up in the battle
Traffic problems likely at crucial stages with 15+ horses wanting prominent positions, particularly dangerous approaching the final three fences
Fitness concerns for The Real Whacker (100 days), Marble Sands (106 days), Perceval Legallois (100 days) and Top Of The Bill (56 days) who may not last the demanding trip
Several reserves including Imperial Saint and Amirite may get late call-ups if any non-runners emerge before the race
Hold-up horses like I Am Maximus and Firefox could benefit significantly if the expected strong pace materializes and prominent runners tire

races.paceDynamic: Bass Hunter, Look Me, The Perfect Poet, Merry Away, Forthfactor, One Knight and Ronnie Russet will ensure a relentless gallop from the off in this competitive Grade 2. With seven confirmed front runners spread across the field, the pace will be genuinely strong throughout the 2m1f journey on testing ground. The sustained tempo will stretch the field and expose any stamina limitations, particularly with the soft going adding extra demands. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses and late finishers who can capitalise on the inevitable pace collapse.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the front runners maintain their aggressive tactics and the gallop stays strong to 2f out
scenarios.body: The relentless early pace will take its toll and create the perfect setup for hold-up horses to pick up the pieces. Stamina and tactical positioning become the decisive factors as the leaders weaken.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Survives Pace
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent racers like Rices Pool or Cooltobecareless gets the perfect pitch just off the leaders
scenarios.body: They can benefit from the strong gallop without doing the donkey work, then strike when the leaders falter in the final furlong. Their forward position gives them first run on the weakening pace-setters.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If the soft ground plays to the stamina strengths of Bass Hunter or Look Me and they can sustain their effort
scenarios.body: One of the established leaders proves best suited to the testing conditions and gallops clear when rivals cry enough. Class and stamina combine to overcome tactical disadvantage.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Tactical Affair
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes moderate due to the large field spreading out or tactical riding
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint finish where positioning and luck in running become crucial factors. The strongest finisher from any position can prevail in a blanket finish.

watchPoints.text: Bass Hunter and Look Me setting unsustainable fractions early could set up the perfect storm for hold-up horses
The ground conditions deteriorating further would heavily favour the stamina types over those needing faster surface
Thelastmanfrompenr and Merlin Allen getting good positions in the rear half as the pace unfolds ahead
Any of the seven front runners trying to restrain early could disrupt the expected strong gallop scenario
Rices Pool and Cooltobecareless securing the ideal prominent pitches just behind the main pace battle
